To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

feeding 30% DDGs to pigs increased the percentage of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) in backfat and decreased the percentage in monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFA), while supplementation with 10g CLA/kg or 1 g betaine/kg reversed these effects.

the diets containing DDGS had no negative impact on growth performance and carcass characteristics, but increased the percentages of PUFA and decreased the percentages of SFA in backfat and bellies fat.
supplementation of CLA or BET could part reverse the effects of 30% DDG on fatty acid profile of backfat and belly in finishing pigs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dietary CLA or BET on the growth performance of pigs fed DDGS.
the effect of dietary CLA or betaine on growth performance, carcasses traits, and fatty acid profile of pigs fed dried distiller grains with solubels (DDGS).
the effects of CLA or BET on the growth performance of pigs fed DDGS, and the effects on fatty acid composition in the backfat or belly fat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
supplementation with CLA and BET in DDGS diets can part reverse the effects of DDGS on carcass fat composition in finishing pigs.
the supplementation of CLA or BET to DDGS-based diets can partially reverse the effects of DDGS on the backfat and bell fat fatty acid composition in finishing pigs.
the addition of CLA or BET to diets containing corn DDGS may be a useful approach for reducing the negative effects on the fatty acid profile of backfat and belly in finishing pigs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diets containing DDGS can increase the PUFA and decrease the SFA in the back fat and belly fat.
the diets containing DDGS had no effect on growth performance, and the increased percentage of PUFA in backfat and the decreased percentage MUFA in belly fat.
CLA or BET may be useful for the management of fat quality in pigs fed DDGS.

the inclusion of DDGS in pig diets is a good alternative to corn, and supplementation with CLA and BET can part reverse the effects of DDGS in carcass fat.
CLA or BET may be useful in the management of carcass fat in DDGS-fed pigs.
